profile.reading:
This is NASK S.A.'s DC 11.11 data center, at ulica 11 Listopada 23A in Warsaw, Poland, a name that comes directly from the street address, 11 Listopada, itself named for Poland's November 11 Independence Day. NASK S.A. describes its Warsaw data center operations as spanning two independent commercial buildings, of which DC 11.11 is the one carrying third party Tier certification. The Telecommunications Industry Association's own certification registry lists an active ANSI/TIA-942-B Constructed Facility Rated 3 certificate for this NASK S.A. site, number TIA942PL231212002, issued December 12, 2023 through certifying body EPI and valid through December 11, 2026, which confirms Tier 3 level design through an independent standards body rather than only NASK's own marketing language. Beyond that certification, NASK's own site describes the facility only in general terms, as offering redundant power, cooling, network, and fire protection systems with three zone physical security, without disclosing a specific IT power capacity in megawatts, a per rack kilowatt figure, or a floor area for this building, an honest gap this registry records rather than a guess.

NASK S.A. is a joint stock company registered with a fully paid share capital of 78,080,612 zloty, and its own materials describe it as having been established by its parent organization, NASK Panstwowy Instytut Badawczy, or NASK State Research Institute, to act as a telecommunications and IT services integrator alongside the parent institute's public mission work. NASK S.A. offers colocation, dedicated servers, infrastructure maintenance under standard and premium support tiers, IaaS and PaaS cloud computing, a public cloud product called nCloud, secure corporate email delivered as software as a service, and file, object, and block storage with backup and disaster recovery, alongside Microsoft license resale. The company also runs nSOC, described on its own site as a competency center providing continuous monitoring of IT and telecommunications infrastructure, a service line consistent with the broader NASK Institute's public focus on cybersecurity, which includes hosting CERT Polska, the country's computer emergency response team, and managing the .pl and .gov.pl domain registries, though those registry and CERT functions belong to the parent research institute rather than to NASK S.A.'s commercial data center business specifically. NASK S.A. maintains additional regional offices in Wroclaw, Gdansk, Katowice, and Kielce beyond its Warsaw headquarters, though its own materials describe only two data centers total, both in Warsaw, rather than a wider national data center footprint. No source checked during this research gave a clear, dated account of when NASK S.A. was formally incorporated as a separate company from its parent institute, or a founding year for the parent institute that this registry could independently verify from a source meeting house style, so those historical details are left out here rather than repeated from unverified secondary claims that appeared in earlier research on this row.

Deliberately dropped the prior draft's claims that NASK PIB was founded in 1991, connected Poland to the internet in 1991, or that NASK S.A. was established in October 2016, since those facts previously rested on Wikipedia and could not be re-confirmed this session from nasksa.pl, nask.pl (the nask.pl institute-history page returned a 404), or any allowed trade press source found via WebFetch (WebSearch quota was exhausted earlier in this session). Power capacity (MW), per-rack kW, and floor area for this specific DC 11.11 building were not found anywhere and are stated as gaps rather than estimated.
